what_happened: A job (2fsa) to re-study firstmate got stuck. The operator tried `athena close` and `athena retry`, and both refused the job. So the operator asked for the same re-study again as a new job (cyvb). This got the work moving, but it was a workaround. It also left the stuck job 2fsa unresolved, and the fix (#106) did not exist yet.
cause: The job lifecycle has states that no command can leave. Close and retry each check their own preconditions, and nothing guarantees that every state allows at least one exit. The 2fsa state fell into the gap between them. The system gave the operator no sanctioned way to recover, so a bypass was the only option. The bypass also leaves the stuck job in place, and two jobs now stand for one request.
prevention: Make the lifecycle total: every non-terminal job state must have at least one allowed exit. At minimum, give `athena close` a force path that works from any state, and have it record the reason. When close or retry refuses a job, the refusal should name the blocking state and the command that would clear it. Add a test that walks every job state and checks that close or retry accepts it. Also let a replacement job be linked to the job it supersedes, so the stuck job is closed automatically.
proposed_request: Make it always possible to get a stuck Athena job out of the way. Today there are job states where both `athena close` and `athena retry` refuse the job (job 2fsa was one), and the operator had to resubmit the work as a new job. The outcome I want: for every job state that is not final, at least one of close or retry succeeds. When a command does refuse, its message says which state blocked it and what to do next. A forced close should work from any state and should record a reason. Add a test that goes through every job state and checks this. Then use the forced close to close job 2fsa as superseded by job cyvb, and confirm that no stale job is left open.
